text:
samir: Observed steady memory growth on a subset of long-context hosts. Not an OOM but KV cache RSS creeps up over 24h for long sessions (>50k tokens). Suspect micro-chunk churn + allocation map fragmentation.

samir: Quick profiling snapshot attached below — it's from a repro run where we kept a single chat open and kept appending.
```
$ kvctl stats --node serve-eu-3 --since 24h
kv_cache/entries: 7.1k
kv_cache/allocated_bytes: 1.9GB
kv_cache/used_bytes: 1.2GB
kv_cache/free_frag_bytes: 700MB
kv_cache/avg_block_size: 272B
kv_cache/small_chunk_allocs: 612k
kv_cache/small_chunk_frees: 611k
kv_cache/compactions: 8
kv_allocator/bucket01_hits: 82%
kv_allocator/bucket02_hits: 9%
kv_allocator/bucket_small_reorgs: 47
```

samir: Notice avg_block_size ~272B and huge small_chunk churn. Frees ~= allocs but free_frag_bytes still high -> allocator internal fragmentation.

claire: Hmm, buckets skewed to bucket01. Are those 256B buckets?

kevin: yep bucket01 == 256B, bucket02 == 1KB. Most keys end up tiny because of long-context KV caching with many short prefixes.

claire: Could be allocator bin packing. If small items are spread across many slabs with mixed occupancy, we end up with lots of holes that can't be reused for larger entries.

samir: Exactly. Hypothesis: repeated append/pop semantics for long contexts cause transient lifetime mismatch -> holes accumulate in 256B slabs, and larger 1KB/4KB slots remain underused.

lee: Any regression signal? Was this recently introduced?

samir: We compared before/after the recent `alloc-map-shadow` change (rolled two weeks ago). Baseline runs showed ~220MB fragmentation; current shows 700MB on same workload. So regression likely correlated.

kevin: alloc-map-shadow reduced lock contention by copying allocation bitmaps on write. It might delay coalescing and make compaction less aggressive.

claire: Could we add an aggressive background buddy-rebalance pass that preferentially targets slabs with >30% holes? Kind of like a per-slab defrag that migrates small survivors to consolidate free spans.

samir: Proposal sketch:
- Track per-slab vacancy waterfall metric (hole_count, largest_contiguous_free).
- If hole_count/lives_ratio > threshold && last_compact > Xs -> schedule local migrate.
- Migration should be incremental: move N small items out, mark slab as candidate, and free once contiguous free >= slab_size/2.
- Limit concurrent migrations per node to avoid spike in CPU/alloc traffic.

kevin: We could reuse existing compaction machinery but add a `micro-migrate` mode tuned for tiny items (<=512B) to avoid moving large KV entries.

claire: Another lever: change small-chunk bin sizes. Current 256B bin may be too fine-grained. If we bump to 384B/512B we might reduce internal fragmentation. But that impacts packing for truly tiny entries.

lee: Bumping bin sizes affects memory layout and could increase wasted space for sub-128B keys. Need simulation.

samir: Ran a quick sim (toy allocator) switching 256->384 and it reduced free_frag_bytes by ~18% on the sample workload but increased avg wasted per tiny-entry by 12B. Overall win in this trace.

kevin: Good. Two orthogonal mitigations then: (1) micro-migrate defrag passes, (2) modest bin coarsening for long-session hosts. Both can be gated behind runtime flags and per-node policies.

claire: For rollout: 1) Add telemetry (per-slab vacancy histogram + migration actions) behind flag. 2) Canary micro-migrate with extremely low concurrency and short TTL. 3) If stable, enable bin-size policy on long-context fleet only.

samir: Also want to add regression test: a long-context replay harness that appends until 100k tokens and asserts fragmentation plateau < 300MB. This will catch alloc-map-shadow regressions.

kevin: Agreed. Who wants to own the initial prototype? I can take the micro-migrate patch and a test harness.

claire: I'll work on the bin-size sim and telemetry dashboards (Console: kv/frag per-node).

lee: I'll provision canary nodes and add the per-node policy toggle in infra-config.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary group 'kv-migrate-v1' created (5 nodes). Monitoring: kv_frag, kv_alloc_qps, cpu_util.

samir: Thanks. Action items:
- kevin: PR with micro-migrate proto + unit tests (ETA 3d)
- claire: bin-size sim + dashboard panels (ETA 4d)
- lee: canary infra + flag (ETA 2d)
- samir: add long-context regression harness + baseline capture (ETA 2d)

claire: One more thought — we should limit migration IO by using ephemeral TLS allocations (avoid copying to disk). Keep it in-mem and backpressure via a migration token bucket.

samir: Yup, token bucket sounds right. Keep total migrated bytes/s <= 10MB/s per node initially.

kevin: I'll include migration throttling and metrics (migrated_bytes, migrate_errors).

lee: Cool. I'll circle back once canary nodes are up.

samir: Great work. If anyone sees other hosts with similar pattern, tag me. :thumbsup:
